title: Staggered-start NCCL fanout analysis for multi-GPU inference
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from a set of runs investigating a recurring throughput/latency regression when scaling inference across 4–16 GPUs (single node and 2-node setups). Hypothesis we iterated on: synchronous collective fanout during KV-cache / attention prefix exchanges is causing transient interconnect saturation and microbursts which degrade tail latency and reduce effective throughput. We explored a lightweight mitigation: staggered-start schedules for tensor/pipeline work and tuned NCCL params (and batching patterns) to smooth out bursts.

Why this matters:
- Production inference must keep p95/p99 latency bounded while maximizing tokens/s.
- Allreduce/collectives used for KV-cache synchronization and pipeline checkpointing show periodic spikes that align with request bursts.
- Simple autoscaling/batching changes mask the problem but don't fix the root cause; need an operational strategy + config knobs for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Experiment goals:
- Reproduce the microburst / tail-latency pattern on lab hardware (A100-80GB on DGX style nodes; also runs on Ampere 4x A100 per node, InfiniBand HDR100).
- Isolate whether issue is: NCCL algorithm choice (ring vs tree/collnet), microbatch scheduling alignment, PCIe/IB contention, or application-level synchronized KV syncs.
- Evaluate staggered-start (small per-GPU offsets) and different NCCL env var combinations for reductions and broadcasts.
- Measure token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, NIC utilization, PCIe counters, and per-GPU interconnect saturation traces.

Test harness & configuration:
- Model: 20B decoder-only transformer (fp16, quantization off for these runs).
- Serving runtime: local build of branch stagger/nccl-tuning (PR 284).
- Modes: tensor-parallel (TP=2,4) + pipeline-parallel simulated by splitting layers across GPUs (pp=1..2), and pure model-shard setups.
- Microbatch sizes: 1, 2, 4, 8 tokens; request concurrency varied from 1 to 64 concurrent requests.
- Hardware sets: single-node 8xA100-80GB (NVLink mesh), 2x-node (2 nodes with 4x A100 each) across HDR IB.
- NCCL variants tested: default, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=ib0, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0/1, NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0/1, NCCL_ALGO= ring/tree (via NCCL_DEBUG info + env where possible). Also tested NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL settings.
- Instrumentation: nvprof/NSys traces, ibstat/ethstats, perf counters for PCIe, and custom tracing in serving runtime to log start/end of collective ops and KV-cache flushes (timestamped).

Key observations:
1) Synchronized collective spikes: 
   - When multiple GPUs initiated KV-syncs at the same tick (common with synchronous request boundary handling), we saw sharp IB utilization spikes (short duration, high amplitude). These aligned with 30–250ms latency spikes for requests that hit during the window.
   - On single node NVLink mesh, the effect exists but is less pronounced; cross-node HDR IB magnifies the p95/p99 impact.

2) NCCL algorithm behavior:
   - Default NCCL picks different algorithms depending on message size. For mid-sized KV blobs (several MB), NCCL used ring algorithms causing many small peer-to-peer transfers. This increased the number of PCIe/IB transactions and increased microburst amplitude.
   - Enabling hierarchical/tree-like collectives (COLLNET / tree) reduced the number of simultaneous peer transfers but sometimes increased latency for large syncs; tradeoff depends on message size distribution.

3) Staggered-start impact:
   - Adding small per-GPU offsets (5–25ms) to collective initiation substantially reduced peak IB utilization and reduced p95 by ~25–40% across several configs. Throughput (tokens/s) often improved as well because tail latency previously limited concurrency.
   - Best offsets depend on batch size/concurrency pattern. Too large offsets reduce overlapping useful work and hurt throughput.

4) Microbatch shapes matter:
   - Smaller microbatch sizes (1–2 tokens) show more frequent collectives; aligning microbatch flushes across GPUs leads to more correlated spikes. Increasing microbatch size reduces frequency of collectives but increases the message size (and can push NCCL into different algorithm regimes).

5) NCCL env tweaks:
   - NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 (disable IB, force TCP over sockets) eliminated IB microbursts but throughput dropped severely for cross-node cases; not acceptable for production.
   - NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=1 helped on 2-node tests with large message sizes – hierarchical collnet reduced simultaneous all-pairs transfers and smoothed NIC load. However collnet requires enabling on all nodes and has kernel/driver-version constraints.
   - Setting NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to restrict which interface NCCL uses improved determinism (important in machines with mgmt interfaces active).

Root cause hypothesis (refined):
- The serving runtime triggers KV-cache synchronization and/or per-layer activation exchanges in a semi-synchronous manner (end-of-microbatch or request boundary). When many shards/GPU tasks reach the same sync point, NCCL launches collectives that produce short, intense bursts on the IB/NVLink fabric. The combination of ring-style algorithms for medium messages and tightly-aligned starts creates many concurrent P2P transfers that saturate links briefly and cause queuing/backpressure in device drivers, raising tail latencies and stalling progress for other requests.

Mitigations tested and recommended:
- Short-term (runtime-level knobs):
  - Staggered-start schedule: add a tiny randomized/staged offset before initiating collectives (configurable: 0–25ms). Default on Dedicated/Private should be conservative (e.g., 8–12ms) and adaptive based on measured p95.
  - Adaptive microbatch coalescing: if concurrency low, flush earlier; if we detect collectives causing spikes, temporarily coalesce to shift the NCCL message-size regime.
  - Rate-limit collective initiations per socket/node: simple token-bucket or semaphore to avoid more than N concurrent large collectives per NIC.

- Medium-term (NCCL + infra):
  - Recommend enabling collnet/tree for cross-node configs where supported; document driver/firmware constraints.
  - Work with infra to ensure NIC firmware/driver versions match NCCL recommendations; enable GDRcopy where available to reduce CPU involvement.
  - Expose NCCL algorithm environment presets in runtime config with profiles (low-latency, high-throughput, balanced).

- Long-term (architecture):
  - Explore partial-KV-consistency / eventual-sync strategies where not all requests need perfectly synchronized KV states; allow lazy or delta-syncs to reduce full-collective frequency.
  - Investigate hybrid allreduce paths: hierarchical aggregation across NVLink within node then IB for inter-node, with adaptive thresholds based on message size and concurrency.

Metric snapshots (representative run):
- Setup: 2 nodes, 4xA100 per node, TP=4, microbatch=2, concurrency=16, 20B model.
- Baseline (no staggering): tokens/s = 12k, p50=30ms, p95=420ms, p99=860ms, IB util median bursts to 95% for 30–80ms windows.
- Staggered start (10ms offsets): tokens/s = 14.3k, p50=28ms, p95=290ms, p99=540ms, IB peak reduced to 70% on same windows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantify cost/benefit across the model size spectrum (7B/70B) and for embedding workloads where KV-sync patterns differ.
- Add deterministic test that triggers worst-case alignment (synthetic workload) to validate mitigation thresholds.
- Measure impact on GPU utilization efficiency when staggering is in place for extremely high concurrency (512+ concurrent small requests).
- Verify NCCL collnet stability across our supported kernel matrix (Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 8 variants, and our older on-prem pilot images).

Action items:
- (Aditi) Add staggered-start option to runtime with config flag and microsecond-resolution jitter; land in feature branch and run nightly perf tests (JIRA-ENG-1723).
- (Samir) Run exhaustive runs for 7B/70B +/- with microbatch sweep and record NCCL debug logs; post raw metrics to the perf S3 bucket.
- (Elena) Validate collnet on infra pilot cluster with current drivers and report compatibility issues (ticket infra-driver-84).
- (Brendan) Draft short ops-runbook with recommended NCCL env presets per deployment profile (hosted/dedicated/private).

Notes to self / informal observations:
- We saw a few runs where a single misconfigured mgmt interface caused NCCL to fallback to an unexpected transport which changed results drastically; keep an eye on socket/interface config.
- There's a subtle interplay between our batching logic and pipeline parallel flushes — when pipeline boundaries align with microbatch flushes you get compounding spikes.
- Early experiments with random small jitter (2–5ms) already showed big wins; seems this is a cheap effective guardrail.

References & artifacts:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/284 (staggered-start prototype + instrumentation hooks)
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-1723 (experiment tracking)
- Confluence: Multi-GPU perf playbook page with current recommended env vars and driver versions.

If this continues to look promising we should:
- Bake a lightweight adaptive algorithm into Redwood Optimize that suggests an offset based on current NIC utilization and request patterns.
- Add a canary rollout in Dedicated where the staggered-start is enabled for a small percentage of requests to measure customer-visible impact before wider rollout.

End of notes.

-- Aditi
